intro.en: School and university words, with several that look like English and mean something else.

nota.en: In an academic context, a course of university studies. It can also mean a race or a person's professional career.

la asignatura.en: the school or university subject; course unit

nota.en: Usually followed by en: matricularse en una asignatura or en un grado.
In Spain, often a state secondary school. ESO is normally for ages 12–16; some institutes also offer optional Bachillerato, usually ages 16–18.

hacer prácticas.en: to do a work placement; internship

nota.en: In Spain, often a primary school. It does not mean a university college.
Most Spanish official Grado programmes have 240 ECTS credits (four academic years); some have 300 or 360.
In Spain, an optional two-year stage, normally for ages 16–18.
As a grade label, aprobado means a pass; the adjective agrees with the noun.
In the usual university grading scale, notable is a grade from 7 to 8.9 out of 10.
In the usual university grading scale, sobresaliente is a grade from 9 to 10 out of 10.

sacar un ocho.en: to get a mark of eight

nota.en: Asistir a means to attend; asistir does not mean to help in this phrase.

titulo.en: The system and its false friends

texto.en:
In Spain, children usually attend primary school at **el colegio**. Compulsory secondary education (**ESO**) normally runs from ages 12 to 16, often at **el instituto**. **Bachillerato** is optional and usually for ages 16 to 18. At university, many students enrol in **un grado**; most degrees have 240 ECTS credits (four academic years), though some are longer. They may continue with **un máster** or **un doctorado**.

University marks use a 0–10 scale: below 5 is **suspenso**; **aprobado** is 5–6.9, **notable** 7–8.9 and **sobresaliente** 9–10.

Useful verbs: **hacer un examen** (sit/take an exam), **aprobar**, **suspender**, **sacar un ocho**, **repasar** and **tomar apuntes**.

Some words can mislead English speakers: **la carrera** is a degree course or programme, not necessarily a professional career; **el colegio** means school, not college; **la asignatura** is a course subject, while **el sujeto** is a grammatical subject; **suspender** an exam means to fail it; **asistir a clase** means to attend class, not to help.

frases.es: He aprobado todo menos una asignatura. He suspendido Estadística.
frases.en: I've passed everything except one subject. I've failed Statistics.

frases.es: ¡Qué pena! ¿Y qué nota has sacado en Historia?
frases.en: What a pity! And what mark did you get in History?

frases.es: Un nueve. Si saco buenas notas, me darán la beca.
frases.en: A nine. If I get good marks, they'll give me the scholarship.

frases.es: Cuando termines la carrera, ¿harás un máster?
frases.en: When you finish your degree, will you do a master's degree?

frases.es: Primero quiero hacer prácticas en una empresa.
frases.en: First I want to do a work placement at a company.

explicacion.en: Suspender an exam is to fail it.

pregunta.en: For a university student, «la carrera» is…

tomado.en: Spanish does not take a mark.

hecho.en: Hacer goes with the exam itself.

termines.en: A future cuando takes the subjunctive.

a research centre.en: That would be un centro de investigación.
